subject: [PATCH v3 3/4] mm: workingset: skip the root memcg flush in workingset_test_recent()

2026-11-14.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the workingset_test_recent() function by skipping the root memory cgroup (memcg) flush when it's not necessary. The function now checks if the eviction memcg is the root memcg, and if so, reads the LRU sizes directly from the node counters instead of flushing the stats. This reduces the overhead of a root flush from 69us to ~150ns on an 80-CPU machine with little cgroup activity. The patch also keeps the flush for reclaim operations as it's still needed to keep up-to-date statistics.

reviews.author: Chris Down
reviews.summary: Identified an opportunity for simplification in the workingset code and suggested using a helper function to reduce code duplication. Approved the patch as is, but noted that adding the helper would improve maintainability.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Joanne,

Joanne Koong writes:
>-	if (flush)
>+	if (flush && !mem_cgroup_is_root(eviction_memcg))
> 		mem_cgroup_flush_stats_ratelimited(eviction_memcg);

Not a big deal, but in the v2 thread you mentioned you would try a
mem_cgroup_flush_lru_stats_ratelimited() helper for this, per Michal's
suggestion. That still seems like a good idea given this skip and the one in
DAMON rely on everything read after them staying in lruvec_use_node_stat(),
and at least speaking for myself, keeping the root check close to the list
in memcontrol.c makes that easier to see. It doesn't need
to hold this patch up though, and I've tested that refaults in the root
cgroup no longer flush, so either way:

Reviewed-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>
Tested-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>

Thanks!

Chris

2026-11-16.patch_summary: This patch series aims to optimize the workingset code by skipping unnecessary flushes of the root memcg in certain scenarios, reducing performance overhead and improving system responsiveness.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong
reviews.summary: Acknowledged Chris's suggestion and proposed an alternative solution by adding a comment to document the dependency, rather than introducing new helper functions.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Chris,

On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 9:07 PM Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name> wrote:
>
> Hi Joanne,
>
> Joanne Koong writes:
> >-      if (flush)
> >+      if (flush && !mem_cgroup_is_root(eviction_memcg))
> >               mem_cgroup_flush_stats_ratelimited(eviction_memcg);
>
> Not a big deal, but in the v2 thread you mentioned you would try a
> mem_cgroup_flush_lru_stats_ratelimited() helper for this, per Michal's
> suggestion. That still seems like a good idea given this skip and the one in
> DAMON rely on everything read after them staying in lruvec_use_node_stat(),
> and at least speaking for myself, keeping the root check close to the list
> in memcontrol.c makes that easier to see. It doesn't need
> to hold this patch up though, and I've tested that refaults in the root
> cgroup no longer flush, so either way:

Thanks for reviewing and testing this series. When I was updating v2
-> v3, I tested out what adding the helper looks like, but found it a
bit overkill. It adds two new api wrappers (one for ratelimited
flushes for workingset, and one for non-ratelimited flushes for
damon), each of which has only one callsite.

Maybe it would be clearest to add a comment directly at the callsites
and above lruvec_use_node_stat() to document the dependency? I'm happy
to add this in, or if you and Michal prefer the helper still, I'm
happy to add the helper APIs.

Thanks,
Joanne
